Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 60, verses 1–3:

It is Madani (revealed at Madinah).

Al-Qurtubi said: "This is the consensus (ijma') of the scholars."

Ibn al-Duraays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Mumtahanah was revealed at Madinah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated the same from Ibn al-Zubayr.

Al-Mumtahinah, with a kasra on the ha', is an active participle (ism fa'il) whose action is attributed to it figuratively (majazan), just as Surat Bara'ah is called al-Fadihah (the Exposer) because it exposes the defects of the hypocrites. It is also said that al-Mumtahanah, with a fatha on the ha', is a passive participle (ism maf'ul), in construct with the woman in whose case it was revealed, who was Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, based on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So test them; Allah knows best their faith﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 10].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The exegetes said: The verse ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, when he wrote to the polytheists of Quraysh about the Prophet's ﷺ march toward them. The story will come at the end of the discussion, if Allah wills. His saying "My enemy" (`aduwwi) is the first object (maf'ul awwal), and "your enemy" (`aduwwakum) is coordinated with it (ma'tuf 'alayhi). The second object is "allies" (awliya'). Allah, glorified is He, attributed the enemy to Himself to magnify their crime. The word "enemy" ('aduww) is a verbal noun (masdar) that applies to the singular, the dual and the plural. The verse indicates the prohibition of allying with the disbelievers in any way.

﴿You convey to them affection﴾: that is, you deliver affection to them. The ba' (in "bil-mawaddah") is either superfluous (za'idah) or causal (sababiyyah).

The meaning is: you convey to them the news of the Prophet ﷺ because of the affection that is between you and them.

Al-Zajjaj said: "You convey to them the news and secret of the Prophet ﷺ through the affection that is between you and them." The clause is in a position of accusative (mahall nasb) as a circumstantial state (hal) from the pronoun in "do not take." It may also be a new independent clause (mustan'afah), intended to inform of what it contains, or to explain their alliance with them. It may also be in an accusative position as a descriptive (sifah) of "allies." The clause ﴿while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth﴾ is in an accusative position as a circumstantial state from the subject of "you convey," or from the subject of "do not take." It may also be a new clause explaining the state of the disbelievers.

The majority read ﴿bima ja'akum﴾ with a single ba' (bi-).

Al-Jahdari and 'Asim, in one narration from him, read "lima ja'akum" with a lam: that is, for the sake of what has come to you of the truth, with the object of disbelief omitted. The sense is: they disbelieved in Allah and the Messenger for the sake of what has come to you of the truth. Or it is by making what is a cause of faith a cause of disbelief, as a rebuke to them.

﴿They expel the Messenger and yourselves﴾: the clause is a new one explaining their disbelief, or it is in an accusative position as a circumstantial state.

His saying ﴿because you believe in Allah, your Lord﴾ is a causal clause for the expulsion: that is, they expel you because of your faith, or out of aversion to your believing.

﴿If you have come out striving in My cause and seeking My pleasure﴾: the answer to the conditional (jawab al-shart) is omitted. That is: if you are such, then do not convey to them affection; or, if you are such, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies. "Jihadan" (striving) and "ibtigha'" (seeking) are in the accusative as causal objects (ʿillah): that is, if you have come out for the sake of striving in My cause and for seeking My pleasure.

The clause ﴿you secretly convey to them affection﴾ is a new clause for censure and rebuke: that is, you secretly convey to them the news because of affection. It is said that it is a substitute (badal) for "you convey." Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that nothing of their conditions is hidden from Him, saying: ﴿And I know best what you conceal and what you reveal﴾. The clause is in an accusative position as a circumstantial state: that is, what you hide and what you show. The ba' in "bima" is superfluous. It is said: "I knew such-and-such," and "I knew of such-and-such." This is on the basis that "a'lam" is an imperfect verb. It is also said that it is a comparative (af'al al-tafdil), meaning: I am more knowing than everyone of what you hide and what you reveal.

﴿Whoever of you does that has indeed strayed from the right path﴾: that is, whoever does that taking My enemy and your enemy as allies and conveys to them affection, has indeed erred from the way of truth and correctness, and has gone astray from the intended path.

﴿If they overcome you, they will be enemies to you﴾: that is, if they encounter you and find you unprepared, they will show you what is in their hearts of enmity. From this comes "mu'athaqah" (contesting/seizing an opportunity), which is seeking to catch an opening in a race. It is also said that the meaning is: if they gain the upper hand over you and gain power over you. The two meanings are close.

﴿And they extend against you their hands and tongues with evil﴾: that is, they extend their hands against you with striking and the like, and their tongues with insult and the like.

﴿And they wish that you would disbelieve﴾: this is coordinated with the answer to the conditional, or with the whole conditional and consequent clause. Abu Hayyan preferred this. The meaning is: they wish for your apostasy and desire your return to disbelief.

﴿Your relatives will not benefit you, nor your children﴾: that is, kinship in its generality will not benefit you, nor will children. He singled them out for mention although they are included in the relatives, to emphasise the love for them and tenderness towards them. The meaning is: these will not benefit you so that you ally with the disbelievers on their account, as happened in the story of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. Rather, what benefits you is what Allah has commanded you: opposing the disbelievers and abandoning alliance with them.

The clause ﴿On the Day of Resurrection He will separate among you﴾ is a new clause explaining that relatives and children will not benefit on that day. The meaning of "yafsilu baynakum" (He will separate among you) is that He will divide you, so that He admits the people of His obedience into Paradise and the people of His disobedience into the Fire.

It is said: the intended meaning of the separation among them is that each of them flees from the other because of the severity of the terror, as in His saying: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother﴾ [Abasa: 34], and the rest of the verse.

It is said: "On the Day of Resurrection" may be connected to what precedes it, meaning: your relatives and children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. Then one stops at that point and begins with His saying ﴿He will separate among you﴾. The preferable view is that it is connected to what follows it, as we have mentioned.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾: nothing of your sayings and actions is hidden from Him, so He will recompense you for that.

The majority read "yufsalu" with a damma on the ya', a light fa' with a fatha, and a fatha on the sad, in the passive voice. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading.

'Asim read with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the sad, in the active voice.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with a damma on the ya', a fatha on the fa' and a kasra on the sad, doubled.

'Alqamah read with the nun.

Qatadah and Abu Haywah read with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the sad, lightly.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, and said: 'Set out until you reach the garden of Khakh, for there is a woman riding with a letter, so take it from her and bring it to me.' We set out until we reached the garden, and there we found the woman riding, and we said: 'Bring out the letter.' She said: 'I have no letter with me.' We said: 'You will bring out the letter or we will strip off your clothes.' So she brought it out from her braid, and we brought it to the Prophet ﷺ. In it was: 'From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to some of the polytheists of Makkah, informing them of some of the affair of the Prophet ﷺ.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'What is this, O Hatib?' He said: 'Do not hasten against me, O Messenger of Allah. I was a man attached to Quraysh, and I was not of them by origin. Those of the Muhajirun who are with you have relatives who protect their families and property in Makkah. So when I missed that connection of lineage among them, I loved to do a favour to them so that they would protect my kin. I did not do this out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'He has spoken the truth.' 'Umar said: 'Let me strike his neck.' He said: 'He witnessed Badr. What will make you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: "Do what you will, for I have forgiven you."' And there was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, conveying to them affection﴾."

There are, on this subject, narrations both connected (musnadah) and incomplete (mursalah) which contain the explanation of this story, and that these verses up to His saying ﴿Indeed there has been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4] were revealed concerning it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 60, verses 10–13 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the ruling concerning the two groups of disbelievers, that goodness and equitable dealing are permitted toward the first group but not the second, He mentioned the ruling concerning those who display faith. He said: ﴿O you who believe, when the believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ from among the disbelievers. This was because the Prophet (ﷺ), when he concluded the treaty with Quraysh at al-Hudaybiyah, agreed to return to them whoever among the Muslims came to him. When women emigrated to him, Allah refused that they be returned to the polytheists, and He commanded that they be tested, saying: ﴿So test them﴾, that is, examine them.

It has been said: he (ﷺ) would make them swear by Allah that they had not left out of hatred for a husband, nor out of desire to move from one land to another, nor in pursuit of worldly gain, but out of love for Allah and His Messenger and desire for his religion. When she swore thus, the Prophet (ﷺ) would give her husband his dower (mahr) and what he had spent on her, and would not return her to him. It has also been said: the testing was that she bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. It has further been said: the testing was only that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite to them the verse: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you﴾ to its end.

It has been said: he (ﷺ) would make them swear by Allah that they had not left out of hatred for a husband, nor out of desire to move from one land to another, nor in pursuit of worldly gain, but out of love for Allah and His Messenger and desire for his religion. The meaning is that whoever has a disbelieving wife, she is not his wife, because her bond has been severed by the difference of religion.

Al-Nakhaʿi said: it refers to a Muslim woman who joins the abode of war and disbelieves. The disbelievers would marry off Muslim men, and Muslim men would marry polytheist women. It has been said: it is general to all disbelieving women, specified by the exclusion of the women of the Book from it.

Al-Qurtubi said: this was specific to that time, in that particular incident, by the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 60, verses 10–13 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the ruling concerning the two groups of disbelievers, that goodness and equitable dealing are permitted toward the first group but not the second, He mentioned the ruling concerning those who display faith. He said: ﴿O you who believe, when the believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ from among the disbelievers. This was because the Prophet (ﷺ), when he concluded the treaty with Quraysh at al-Hudaybiyah, agreed to return to them whoever among the Muslims came to him. When women emigrated to him, Allah refused that they be returned to the polytheists, and He commanded that they be tested, saying: ﴿So test them﴾, that is, examine them.

It has been said: he (ﷺ) would make them swear by Allah that they had not left out of hatred for a husband, nor out of desire to move from one land to another, nor in pursuit of worldly gain, but out of love for Allah and His Messenger and desire for his religion. When she swore thus, the Prophet (ﷺ) would give her husband his dower (mahr) and what he had spent on her, and would not return her to him. It has also been said: the testing was that she bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. It has further been said: the testing was only that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite to them the verse: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you﴾ to its end.

The scholars differed over whether women were included in the truce (ʿahd al-hudnah) or not, on two opinions. According to the opinion that they were included, this verse specifies (mukhassisah) that covenant, and this is the view of most scholars.

According to the opinion that they were not included, there is neither abrogation (naskh) nor specification. ﴿Allah knows best their faith﴾: this clause is parenthetical (muʿtaridah), to explain that the true reality of their condition is known only to Allah, glorified is He, and He did not impose upon you knowledge of it. He only imposed upon you the testing of them, so that what indicates the truthfulness of their claim of desire for Islam may become apparent to you. ﴿Then if you know them to be believers﴾, that is, you know this outwardly (biḥasab al-ẓāhir) after the testing that you were commanded to carry out, ﴿do not return them to the disbelievers﴾, that is, to their disbelieving husbands. The clause ﴿They are not lawful to them, nor are they lawful to them﴾ gives the reason for the prohibition against returning them.

In this is evidence that a believing woman is not lawful to a disbeliever, and that the woman's conversion requires her separation from her husband, not merely her emigration. The repetition serves to emphasize the prohibition, or the first clause indicates the dissolution of the marriage and the second the impermissibility of a new marriage. ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾, that is, give the husbands of those who emigrated and embraced Islam the equivalent of what they spent on them as dowers.

Al-Shafiʿi said: if a person other than the husband, from her relatives, seeks her, he is prevented from taking her without compensation. ﴿And there is no blame upon you for marrying them﴾, because they have become of your religion, ﴿when you have given them their compensation (ujūr)﴾, that is, their dowers. This is after the completion of their waiting period (ʿiddah), as the evidence for the obligation of the waiting period indicates. ﴿And do not hold to marriage with disbelieving women﴾.

Most readers recited ﴿tumsikū﴾ with a light (takhfīf) pronunciation, from imsāk (holding). Abu ʿUbayd preferred this reading, because of His saying: ﴿then retain them in good manner﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]. Al-Hasan, Abu al-ʿAliyah and Abu ʿAmr read it with a doubled (tashdīd) pronunciation, from tamassuk (clinging). ʿIṣam is the plural of ʿiṣmah, which is that by which one holds fast, and what is meant here is the bond (ʿiṣmah) of the marriage contract.

The meaning is that whoever has a disbelieving wife, she is not his wife, because her bond has been severed by the difference of religion.

Al-Nakhaʿi said: it refers to a Muslim woman who joins the abode of war and disbelieves. The disbelievers would marry off Muslim men, and Muslim men would marry polytheist women. Then this was abrogated (nusikha) by this verse. This applies specifically to polytheist women, not to disbelieving women from the People of the Book.

It has been said: it is general to all disbelieving women, specified by the exclusion of the women of the Book from it.

The majority of scholars have held that…

Some scholars said: they are separated by the mere conversion of the husband. This applies only when the woman has been consummated. As for when she has not been consummated, there is no disagreement among the scholars that the bond between them is severed by Islam, since she has no waiting period.

﴿And ask for what you have spent﴾, that is, demand the dowers of your wives who have gone over to the disbelievers. ﴿And let them ask for what they have spent﴾. The exegetes said: whoever among the Muslim women apostatized and went over to the disbelievers of the people of the treaty, the disbelievers would be told: give back her dower. And the Muslims would be told: when a woman from the disbelievers comes to the Muslims and embraces Islam, return her husband's dower to her disbelieving husband. ﴿That is the judgment of Allah﴾, that is, that which has been mentioned, the return of dowers from both sides, is the judgment of Allah. His saying ﴿He judges among you﴾ is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) or it is a resumed (mustaʾnafah) clause.

﴿And Allah is Knowing, Wise﴾: that is, of profound knowledge, nothing hidden from Him is concealed, of profound wisdom in His statements and actions.

Al-Qurtubi said: this was specific to that time, in that particular incident, by the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Muslims.

﴿And if any of your wives have gone from you to the disbelievers﴾. When the preceding verse was revealed, the Muslims said: we accept the judgment of Allah. They wrote to the polytheists, but they refused. Then there was revealed His saying: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone from you to the disbelievers﴾, of what you gave them of the dowers of the Muslim women. It has been said: the meaning is: if one of your women escapes to the disbelievers by her apostasy as a Muslim woman. ﴿Then you take booty (fa-ʿāqabtum)﴾. Al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: fa-ʿāqabtum means fa-ghanimtum, you took booty. Al-Zajjaj said: its interpretation is that the outcome (ʿuqbā) became yours, that is, the spoils became yours until you took booty. ﴿Then give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they spent﴾, from the dowers of the emigrant women whom they married, and deliver it to the disbelievers, and do not give it to their disbelieving husbands.

Qatadah and Mujahid said: they were commanded to give those whose wives had gone the equivalent of what they had spent from the fay' (spoils without battle) and the booty (ghanimah). This verse is abrogated; its ruling ceased after the conquest.

The summary of its meaning is that ﴿from your wives﴾ may be connected to ﴿has gone from you﴾, that is, from the side of your wives, and by "thing" is meant the dower which the husband paid. It may also be connected to an omitted element as a description of "thing". Then in "thing" it may be meant the dower, but in this case there must be an omitted genitive, that is, "from the dowers of your wives", so that the described and its description agree. It may also be meant by "thing" the women, that is, a kind and category of them, and this is the apparent sense of His saying ﴿from your wives﴾ and His saying ﴿those whose wives have gone﴾. The meaning is that they give to whoever's wife has gone to the polytheists and disbelieved, and the polytheists did not return her dower to him, as Allah has judged, the equivalent of that dower which he spent on her, from the booty.

﴿And fear Allah in whom you believe﴾, that is, beware of exposing yourselves to anything that brings punishment upon you, for the faith with which you are characterized requires this of its possessor.

﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾, that is, intending to pledge allegiance to you upon Islam, ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾ of things, whatever it may be. This took place on the day of the conquest of Makkah, when the women of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pledge allegiance to him. Allah commanded him to take from them that they would not associate partners, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, which was what the Jahiliyyah used to do, burying daughters alive. ﴿Nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾, that is, they will not attribute to their husbands a child who is not theirs.

Al-Farra' said: a woman would pick up a newborn and say to her husband: this is my child from you. That is the slander invented between their hands and feet, because when the mother gives birth the child falls between her hands and feet. What is meant here is not that she attributes her child of fornication to her husband, for that falls under the prohibition of adultery.

﴿Nor disobey you in what is right﴾, that is, in every matter that is obedience to Allah.

ʿAtaʾ said: in every act of righteousness and piety. The two Muqatils said: by "what is right" is meant the prohibition against wailing, tearing clothes, cutting hair, tearing the collar, scratching faces, and calling for destruction. Qatadah, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, Muhammad ibn al-Saʾib, and Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise. But the meaning of the Qur'an is broader than what they said.

It has been said: the reason for restricting it to "what is right," although he (ﷺ) only commands what is right, is to alert that obedience to a creature is not permissible in disobedience to the Creator. ﴿So accept their pledge﴾ is the answer to "when" (idhā). The meaning: when they pledge allegiance to you upon these matters, then accept their pledge. He did not mention in their pledge the prayer, zakah, fasting, or hajj, because it is clear that these and similar matters are pillars of the religion and rites of Islam. He singled out the matters mentioned because they most frequently occur among women. ﴿And ask Allah's forgiveness for them﴾, that is, seek from Allah forgiveness for them after this pledge they have made to you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, that is, of profound forgiveness and mercy toward His servants.

﴿O you who believe, do not make allies of a people with whom Allah is angry﴾. They are all groups of disbelief. It has been said: specifically the Jews. It has been said: specifically the hypocrites. Al-Hasan said: the Jews and the Christians.

The first is preferable, because all groups of disbelief share the characteristic that Allah, glorified is He, is angry with them. ﴿They have despaired of the Hereafter﴾: "min" here indicates the starting point of the act (li-ibtidāʾ al-ghāyah), that is, they do not believe in the Hereafter at all because of their disbelief. ﴿As the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves﴾, that is, as their despair regarding the resurrection of their dead, because of their belief that there is no resurrection. It has been said: as the disbelievers who have died among them have despaired of the Hereafter, because they have come to know the reality and know that they have no share in the Hereafter. In that case "min" in the first view is initial (ibtidāʾiyyah), and in the second it is explanatory (bayāniyyah). The first is preferable.

Al-Bukhari transmitted from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam that "when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant with the disbelievers of Quraysh at al-Hudaybiyah, believing women came to him, and Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ until His saying ﴿and do not hold to marriage with disbelieving women﴾, so Umar, on that day, divorced two women who had been his wives in polytheism."

He also transmitted it from both of them by a longer version, in which it says: "Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿit was among those who went out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she was an adult woman. Her family came asking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to return her to them, until Allah revealed about the believing women what He revealed."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying ﴿So test them﴾ that he said: their testing was that they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. When they knew that this was true from them, they were not returned to the disbelievers, and her husband among the disbelievers with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made a covenant was given her dower which he had paid her, and they were made lawful to the believers when they gave them their compensation.

Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted from him, who said: the Surah al-Mumtahanah was revealed after that truce. Whoever of their women embraced Islam, she was asked: what brought you out? If she had gone out fleeing from her husband and out of aversion to him, she was returned. If she had gone out out of desire for Islam, she was retained and what he had spent was returned to her husband.

Ibn Abi Usamah, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted with a good chain (isnad), as al-Suyuti said, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying ﴿When believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them﴾ that he said: when a woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ), Umar ibn al-Khattab would make her swear by Allah that she had not left out of desire for a land other than her land; by Allah that she had not left out of hatred for a husband; by Allah that she had not left in pursuit of worldly gain; and by Allah that she had not left except out of love for Allah and His Messenger.

Ibn Mani' transmitted through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab embraced Islam, and his wife remained among the polytheists, so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not hold to marriage with disbelieving women﴾.

Al-Shawkani, *Fath al-Qadir*, commentary on Surah 60, verses 10–13 (part 2 of 2):

It was narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh, from ʿAishah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would test those women believers who emigrated to him with this verse: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you...﴾ up to his words ﴿...Forgiving, Merciful﴾. Whoever among the believing women acknowledged this condition, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to her: "I have accepted your allegiance by word alone." By Allah, his hand never touched the hand of any woman among those he took the pledge from. He pledged them only with his words: "I have accepted your allegiance to that."

It was narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Manṣur, Ibn Saʿd, Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, al-Nasaʾi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh, from Umaymah bint Ruqaiqah, who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a group of women to pledge allegiance to him. He took our pledge concerning what is in the Qur'an: that we would not associate anything with Allah, up to his words ﴿and not disobey you in what is right﴾. He said: 'In what you are able and capable of.' We said: 'Allah and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves. O Messenger of Allah, will you not shake our hands?' He said: 'I do not shake hands with women. My word to a hundred women is the same as my word to one woman.'" There are other narrations on this subject.

It was narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and others, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) and he said: 'Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery.' He then recited the verse about women. 'Whoever among you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of these and is punished in this world, that is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of these and Allah conceals it, then it is up to Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated through Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿nor bring a slander that they have invented﴾, that he said: "A free woman would give birth to a girl, and she would substitute a boy in her place."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him concerning the verse, that he said: "It means: they should not attribute to their husbands children who are not theirs. ﴿And not disobey you in what is right﴾: it is a condition that Allah laid down for women."

Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah, who said: "A woman among the women said: 'What is this right thing (maʿruf) in which we must not disobey you?' He said: 'Do not wail (niyahah).' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the family of so-and-so helped me with my uncle, and I must repay them for it.' He refused me, so I went back to him several times until he permitted me to repay them. But I did not wail after that, and none of the women remained except that she wailed, apart from me."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Umm ʿAtiyyah, who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited to us that we would not associate anything with Allah, and he forbade us from wailing (niyahah). A woman among us withdrew her hand and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, so-and-so helped me, and I want to repay her.' He said nothing to her. She went away and then came back, and said: 'None of us kept her pledge except Umm Sulaym, Umm al-ʿAlaʾ, and the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Muʿadh,' or 'the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Muʿadh.'"

Many hadiths have been related prohibiting wailing (nawh).

Abu Ishaq and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr and Zayd ibn al-Harith used to befriend a man from the Jews. So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾ the verse."

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani narrated from Ibn Masʿud concerning His words ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾, that he said: "They do not believe in it nor hope for it, as the disbeliever despairs when he dies and sees its reward and looks upon it."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning the verse, that he said: "They are the disbelievers, the people of the graves, who have despaired of the Hereafter."

Ibn Jarir narrated from him concerning the verse, that he said: "Whoever among those who disbelieved has died, the living among those who disbelieved have despaired that they will return to them or that Allah will resurrect them."
